intent: A formal scholarly treatment: a claim supported by transparent method and citation, hedged precisely rather than confidently overstated.

register.default: Formal and method-transparent. A hedge is a correct description of what the evidence supports, not a weakness to be edited toward confidence.
avoid: confident phrasing that outruns what the method supports
citation used as decoration rather than as a load-bearing claim of what the cited work found
informal register borrowed from suengj-com's other content types

evidence_burden.rationale: The highest citation burden of any content type: a scholarly claim is only as strong as the method and the literature trail behind it, and must confront material that could narrow it.

typical_structure: Conclusion bounded strictly by the evidence
flexibility: Structure is a default; the method section and the limitations section may not be omitted, because both are what makes a hedge checkable rather than decorative.
anti_patterns: Overstating confidence beyond what the stated method supports
Omitting method detail needed for a reader to assess validity
Treating a correctly hedged claim as weak prose and editing the hedge away — a correctly hedged claim is stronger than an overstated one
Citing a source without checking that it actually says what it is cited for

quality_gates.rationale: Highest floor of any content type: a scholarly claim is only as strong as the method and citation trail carried in the prose that argues from it.

semantic_roles.rationale: Method and evidence carry the argument; procedural or code blocks are rarely the load-bearing unit in a scholarly claim.
